sentences.text: Ardeadactylus is an extinct pterosaur named after the heron and finger, found in the Upper Jurassic Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, southern Germany.
Scientists suspect it was a heron-like animal with a long neck and long legs that ate fish.
The neotype specimen has an estimated wingspan of 1.45 meters, while another specimen is about 10% larger.
The original holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was found near Eichstätt in 1853 and acquired by Professor Ludwig Frischmann for the Herzoglich Leuchtenbergische Naturalien-Kabinett.
Only two specimens of Ardeadactylus currently exist: one found in 1874 initially thought to be Pterodactylus suevicus, and a neotype held at the Jura Museum in Eichstätt.
The destruction of the original holotype during World War II led Peter Wellnhofer to designate a neotype in 1970.
Ardeadactylus had fewer but larger teeth than Pterodactylus antiquus, suggesting it may have preyed on larger fish.
The genus Ardeadactylus was established by Bennett et al. in 2013.
The species Ardeadactylus longicollum was originally described by von Meyer in 1854.
A 2017 analysis placed Ardeadactylus in the family Aurorazhdarchidae as a sister taxon to Aurorazhdarcho.
Ardeadactylus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.
A 2018 analysis by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues recovered Ardeadactylus within the family Ctenochasmatidae instead of Aurorazhdarchidae.
